task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm having trouble sending picture messages — MMS, I think they're called. It's been a few hours now and nothing goes through. Can you help me figure it out?

turns.thought:
I'd be happy to help you troubleshoot picture messaging. First, I need to pull up your account so I can check your line.

Could you please provide your phone number (or your account/customer ID)? If you'd prefer, I can also look you up by your full name and date of birth.
turns.execution_output: User: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
(<thinking>The user has three lines. Let me finish inspecting the remaining line so I can identify which line is actually associated with the number he provided and whether any line is suspended.

Let me call get_details_by_id for L1003 to complete the picture.</think:6124c78e>

I found your account. Let me start diagnosing the picture-messaging issue.

Could you please check the following on your phone and tell me what you see?

1. Open your phone's **Messages** app and try sending a picture message, then tell me if it fails (this runs a check on whether MMS can send).
2. Look at the **status bar** at the top of your screen — what icons do you see (signal bars, 5G/4G/LTE, Wi-Fi, airplane mode, etc.)?
turns.execution_output: User: I'll try sending a picture message first.

turns.thought:
That's exactly the problem — Airplane Mode is ON, which disconnects all wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so picture messages can't go through.

Please do this on your phone:

1. Swipe down from the top of your screen to open **Quick Settings** (on some phones, swipe down twice).
2. Find the **Airplane Mode** tile and tap it so it turns **OFF** (grey/disabled).
   - If you don't see it there, go to **Settings → Network & Internet** (or **Connections**) and toggle **Airplane Mode** off.
3. Wait about 10–20 seconds for your phone to reconnect.

Then check your status bar again — you should now see signal bars and a network type like 5G/LTE. After that, try sending the picture message again.

Let me know what the status bar shows once Airplane Mode is off, and whether the picture message goes through.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn airplane mode off.

turns.thought:
Good — your cellular service is back now since you have signal bars and 5G. Since MMS still isn't working, I need to check a few more things on your phone. Please do the following and tell me what you see:

1. Check your **mobile data** status — go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network** (or check your network status) and tell me whether Mobile Data is turned ON.
2. Check your **mobile data restriction** settings — look for **Data Saver** (Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver) and tell me if it's ON or OFF.
3. Check your **network type** — in the status bar or settings, does it show 5G, LTE/4G, 3G, or 2G?

Also, what exactly happens when you try to send the picture message now — does it fail immediately, spin/stall, or show a red exclamation mark? That will help narrow it down.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check those settings.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's very likely the issue! I checked your line (555-123-2002), and it **is** roaming-enabled on our side, so you're covered for international use. The problem is on the phone itself: **Data Roaming is turned OFF**.

When you're outside your home network (like in France right now), your phone will refuse to use mobile data unless Data Roaming is turned on. Since picture messages (MMS) require mobile data, they'll just sit there and never send — exactly what you're seeing.

Please turn it on:

1. Open **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network** (on some phones: **Settings → Connections → Mobile networks**).
2. Find **Roaming** or **Data roaming** and toggle it **ON** (you may get a warning about charges — your line is provisioned for roaming, so it's fine to accept).
3. Wait a few seconds for the phone to register on the French network.

Then please:
- Check your status bar/network status again to confirm mobile data is connected.
- Try sending the picture message once more.

Let me know what happens — if it still doesn't go through, we'll check the MMS settings (APN/MMSC) next.
turns.execution_output: User: That makes sense. Let me turn data roaming on.

turns.thought:
I understand the frustration — we've ruled out the two most common causes (airplane mode and roaming), so let's look at the MMS-specific settings next. Two quick checks:

**1. Does general internet work?**
Open your browser (or an app like email) and try loading a page using mobile data (turn Wi-Fi off, which it already is). Tell me whether that works. This tells us whether it's a general data problem or something specific to picture messages.

**2. Check your APN settings:**
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Advanced → Access Point Names (APN)**.
  - (On some phones: **Settings → Connections → Mobile networks → Access point names**.)
- Tap the active/selected APN (it should have a dot or checkmark next to it).
- Tell me:
  - What the **APN** name/value shows, and
  - What the **MMSC** field shows (this is the server address used for picture messages — it usually looks like a web address).

If the MMSC field is blank or looks wrong, that alone would stop picture messages from sending even with a perfect data connection.

In the meantime, while you check: since you just turned data roaming on, it can take a few moments for the phone to register fully on the French network — so if you haven't yet, please toggle mobile data off and back on (or reboot the phone) and retry the picture message.

Let me know what you find for those two checks and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the APN settings first.

turns.thought:
Good news: your data connection is working well (275 Mbps is excellent), and your MMSC URL **is** set, so that's not blank. Since general internet works but picture messages don't, let's move to the remaining MMS-specific causes.

Please check these next:

**1. Wi-Fi Calling** — it can sometimes interfere with picture messaging:
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Calls & SMS → Wi-Fi Calling** (or **Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi Calling**).
- Tell me whether it's ON or OFF. If it's **ON**, please toggle it **OFF**, then wait a few seconds and try sending the picture message again.

**2. Messaging app permissions** — the app needs storage (for the photo) and SMS permissions:
- Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages (or your messaging app) → Permissions**.
- Tell me whether **Storage/Photos and videos** and **SMS** are set to **Allow**. If either is denied, please set them to **Allow**.

Let me know what you find for both, and whether the picture message sends after making those changes. If it still won't go, the next step is resetting your APN settings to default (which refreshes the MMS server address) followed by a phone reboot.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the Wi-Fi calling status first.

turns.thought:
You're very welcome — glad we got it sorted out!

To recap what fixed it:
- **Airplane Mode** was on (no service at all) → turned off
- **Data Roaming** was off → turned on (your line 555-123-2002 is provisioned for roaming)
- **Wi-Fi Calling** was interfering with MMS → turned off, and that resolved it

Regarding your questions:

**Data roaming:** Yes — keep it on for the rest of your trip. You're outside your home network in France, and with data roaming off your phone won't use mobile data at all, which would also block picture messages.

**Wi-Fi Calling:** The only guidance I have on this is that it can interfere with picture messaging while roaming, and turning it off resolved your issue. I'd leave it off while you're abroad and need to send picture messages. Beyond that, I'm not able to advise on when you should switch it back on — that's a settings preference I can't make a recommendation on. If you do turn it back on later and picture messages stop working again, that's the first thing to check.

One important note: since you'll be roaming, please be aware that your line's plan has a 15 GB data limit for the current cycle (ending 2025-02-28), and you've used 8.7 GB so far. If you hit the limit, data — and picture messaging — will stop working again. If that happens, contact me and we can look at adding data or plan options.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?
turns.execution_output:
User: That all makes sense — I'll keep data roaming on and leave Wi-Fi calling off while I'm here. Good to know about the data limit too; sounds like I've got some room left, so I should be fine for the rest of the trip.

No, that's everything — picture messages are working again, which is what I needed. Thanks again for all your help!
